title: Brazilian superfan in S'pore rallying 500-strong crowd for Brazil vs Japan match at The Kallang on Nov. 14

 Brazilian superfan in S'pore rallying 500-strong crowd for Brazil vs Japan match at The Kallang on Nov. 14
 Will Brazil win Japan again?
 Zhangxin Zheng 
 November 13, 2026, 03:49 PM
Photo from Ana Paula Nielsen's Instagram and The Kallang.
 If you're still on the fence about catching the Brazil vs Japan friendly at The Kallang this Saturday (Nov. 14), one Brazilian superfan in Singapore has a simple message for you: you're not just buying a ticket, you're investing in a core memory. 
 Meet the force behind Singapore's Brazilian community: Ana Paula Nielsen. 
 Ana is a longtime resident of nearly 14 years who has spent the last decade bringing her homeland's vibrant spirit to Singapore, from leading Chingay contingents to organising annual Brazilian carnival parties . 
 Photo courtesy of Ana Paula Nielsen. Viva Brasil contingent at 2026 Chingay.
 Photo courtesy of Ana Paula Nielsen (second from the right). Photo of 2026 Viva Brasil carnival.
 Recently, she has been gearing up for Saturday's headline clash at the National Stadium. 
 At least 400 to 500 Brazilians in Singapore are expected to turn up in full force to cheer on their national team. 
 Ana shared that Brazilians from Malaysia and neighbouring countries will also be coming to Singapore for this match, bringing the total estimated number to 700 to 800. 
 Photo from Ana Paula Nielsen's Instagram. Photo of Ana (on the right), her co-creator behind Brasileiros em Singapura, Beatriz Barreto (left), and a Japanese journalist who's been following Brazil since 1998.
 "How much is the memory worth?"
 Tickets for the Mizuho Blue Challenge match range from S$98 to S$888 , which admittedly isn't cheap. 
 But to her, the price tag is worth every cent. 
 "It's not spending money [on the tickets], it's an investment," she shared, pointing out that fans rarely get the chance to watch world-class Brazilian stars live in Singapore. 
 She speaks from experience. Back at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, Ana took her two young daughters to a match where Neymar scored four goals. 
 Video of Ana appearing on TV showing World Cup 2014. Video of Ana Paula Nielsen.
 Because of where they were seated near the tunnel, she ended up getting a flag signed by Kaká as the players walked past. 
 "I don't remember how much I paid for the tickets," she laughed. "What you remember are the moments... to tell in the future to your grandkids."
 Not just a football match
 Those heading down to The Kallang on Nov. 14 won't just be watching a high-stakes rematch of the 2026 World Cup Round of 32, where Brazil edged out Japan 2-1. 
 They'll also be treated to the infectious energy of Singapore's Brazilian community. 
 Ana personally reached out to The Kallang to offer the community's full support and added that attendees can expect some "activations". 
 "I told The Kallang to count on us, not only on spreading the word."
 With the experience of bringing 430kg of authentic carnival costumes from Rio to Singapore for Chingay and throwing annual parties complete with 50kg of confetti and live samba drumming, Ana and the Brazilian community know a thing or two about creating an electric atmosphere. 
 Ana is hoping for a 4-0 Brazil win on Saturday, repeating their 2014 friendly victory over Japan in Singapore. 
 Mizuho Blue Challenge: Brazil vs Japan
 When: Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026 
 Time: Kick-off at 6:15pm 
 Where: National Stadium, The Kallang 
 Tickets available here .
